subject: Dedicated cluster configuration options for ElaraOps
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@elara-labs.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: solutions@elara-labs.com
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cluster sizing and min-commit options for ElaraOps

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the call this morning. ElaraOps is moving our document-understanding inference workloads into production in Q4 and we need a clear set of reservation options to take to procurement. High-level:
- Expected steady-state: ~120 qps at 512 token context for our distilled model (mixed precision).
- Peak bursts: up to ~320 qps for short windows (2–6 hours) during batch ingestion.
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for user-facing endpoints.

What we need from Redwood: three concrete reservation choices that show cluster size, minimum guaranteed GPUs, projected warmup timeline (ramp schedule), and fallback/burst behavior. Procurement also wants an explicit statement of what triggers overage pricing vs. burst credits.

Attached is a short requirements doc (elara-inference-requirements-2028.pdf). Can you send a short proposal we can present internally by EOD Tuesday?

Appreciate it —
Carlos
Head of Platform
Elara Labs
From: chloe_martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@elara-labs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cluster sizing and min-commit options for ElaraOps

Hi Carlos —

Thanks for the brief and the attachment. I put together three discrete reservation options below (summary first, details after) and attached a one-page proposal (chloe-proposal-v1.pdf) you can drop into the procurement packet. Quick ask: confirm whether the distilled model uses static 512-token contexts for the majority of calls or if there is a wide variance (that affects KV-cache behavior and effective throughput).

Summary (high level)
• Option 1 — Safety net / Pilot: 8 GPUs (reserved), warm pool enabled. Designed for low-commit proofs and short pilot. Supports steady-state ~40–60 qps; bursts to ~120 qps with pre-warmed pool. 45-day ramp to steady throughput.
• Option 2 — Baseline production: 24 GPUs (reserved), 8-GPU burst capability. Supports steady-state ~120 qps with headroom for 200 qps bursts. 60-day ramp with staged activations (8 → 16 → 24).
• Option 3 — Aggressive runway: 48 GPUs (reserved), 20-GPU burst capacity + geo-bursting. Targets steady-state up to 200 qps and sustained peaks to 320 qps. 90-day ramp with canary + full fleet activation.

Detailed notes and assumptions
- Model / perf assumptions: numbers assume your distilled model runs at ~1.6 tokens/ms per A100-equivalent GPU at 512 tokens. If you send an internal perf sample we can tighten these.
- Warmup and prefix caching: to hit burst targets we recommend enabling prefix caching for the most common prompts and keeping a small warm pool (size noted above). Warm pool incurs a modest incremental monthly fee but dramatically reduces p95.
- Ramp schedule: ramp windows assume Redwood can pre-allocate capacity in our shared pool and warm the cluster. We will phase activation by pod (8–GPU pods) and can shift the second phase earlier if needed.
- Overage and burst: baseline chargeable overage applies after reserved capacity + burst credits are exhausted. Burst credits are applied automatically for the first X hours/month as defined in the contract; beyond that real-time overage pricing (per-GPU-hour) applies. We can include a capped overage rate if procurement prefers a hard upper bound.

Next steps
1) Confirm token context variance and any regular long-tail prompts.
2) Which of the three options you want priced (we can return line-item pricing + activation calendar).
3) If procurement needs a cap on overage, tell us the acceptable cap and we’ll sketch the contract language.

I attached chloe-proposal-v1.pdf with a compact table showing the activation timeline (week-by-week) and expected latency/throughput targets per option. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the table.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: chloe-proposal-v1.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@elara-labs.com>, chloe_martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cluster sizing and min-commit options for ElaraOps

Carlos — quick follow from pricing. A few practical clarifications and what we can do on the pricing deck:

- Option pricing: we’ll return net pricing for each option including reserved GPU-hours, burst credits allocation, and a line for warm-pool buffer (monthly).
- SLA / credits: the Baseline production (24 GPU) option comes with a standard 99.9% uptime SLA. Aggressive runway (48 GPU) can be elevated to 99.95% with a premium add-on.
- Procurement-friendly cap: we can offer a soft overage cap for the first 3 months (we’ll absorb charges above the cap up to a negotiated threshold), then revert to standard overage. This is useful during your ramp window.

Action items from my side: I’ll upload a pricing worksheet to the HubSpot deal and include a short note on contract clauses for burst credits and overage caps. Chloe — can you confirm the staged activation weeks (I want to ensure our capacity ops team has a heads-up for the pod activations)?

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ELARA-527
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@elara-labs.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cluster sizing and min-commit options for ElaraOps

Thanks Chloe and Ben — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and infra:

1) Minimum commit question: for Option 2 (24 GPUs) is the hard minimum 24 GPUs for the entire term, or can we structure a 16→24 guaranteed ladder where the first 3 months are 16 guaranteed then step to 24? Procurement prefers staged guarantees tied to milestone KPIs.

2) Overage cap: procurement likes the soft overage cap for the first 90 days. Can you confirm the cap number (example: $10k/month) and whether Redwood would absorb anything beyond that for the pilot ramp?

3) Ramp acceleration: our infra team is asking if we can shift the staged activation to 4 weeks instead of 8 for the second phase — essentially 8 → 16 in week 2, then 24 in week 4 — to support an accelerated customer pilot. What are the operational implications for warm-pool readiness and SLA transition?

On the compliance side: SOC2 evidence is needed for procurement. Monica — can you drop the SOC2 packet (or a link) into the HubSpot deal?

If you can reply with a short note answering the three items above we’ll assemble a one-page recommendation for our execs and set a procurement call for Friday.

Appreciate it —
Carlos
